appraisal_events.evidence: the narrator's extended commentary on how egoists always have the last word, treating those who move them to pity as the guilty party, so that their own hardness can reach extreme cruelty without troubling their conscience
appraisal_events.explanation: The narrator directly diminishes Robert by exposing the self-serving logic behind his reproaches to his mother, framing his resistance to her plea as a form of egoism verging on cruelty.

appraisal_events.evidence: she stops insisting because she senses she can no longer hold him back, then tells the narrator she is sure she caused him pain, that mothers are very selfish, and that she wishes she could catch him to say she is not angry and that he was right
appraisal_events.explanation: Mme de Marsantes yields ground to her son, abandons her own claim on his time, and turns the blame onto herself, giving Robert the emotional upper hand in the exchange.

status_effects.explanation: The narrator's aphorism about egoists is applied directly to Robert, exposing his self-justifying hardness toward his mother.
His mother's capitulation and self-blame leave Robert holding the emotional advantage in the relation, unresisted and unreproached.
She gives up her claim on her son, absolves him, and blames her own selfishness instead, visibly the more yielding and pained party.
